small_guidance:
- The current kernel reloads the same input window pixels four times (x_base, +1, +IW, +IW+1). Restructure to load a single (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N+stride) tile of x covering both pooled positions and reuse via 4 dot products with the same w — this halves global loads and is a pure tuning-level change.
- Add autotune configs with larger BLOCK_N (e.g. 128, 256) since OUT_SPATIAL = 63*63 ≈ 3969 and OC=128 is small — bias toward BLOCK_M=32/64 with BLOCK_N=128/256 at num_warps=8, num_stages=2. Drop the BLOCK_M=256 configs (OC only 128).
- Prune unused autotune configs; many of the listed ones can never win for (OC=128, OUT_SPATIAL≈4000, K_TOTAL=576). Keep ~5 configs to cut autotune overhead.
large_guidance:
- Switch to channels-last (NHWC) layout for both input and output so the GEMM-K axis (IC) is contiguous. Currently the inner loop strides across IC*IH*IW per K element causing non-coalesced loads; NHWC makes the IC reduction a contiguous vector load per spatial pixel.
- Reformulate as: program tile over (N, pooled_h tile, pooled_w tile, OC tile); accumulate the full conv output for the 2x2 pre-pool window in registers as 4 GEMM accumulators sharing one weight load and one shared im2col gather of a (2+KH-1)x(2+KW-1) input patch — eliminates the 4x redundant x loads in the current design.
- Consider a persistent-CTA design that iterates over (n, oc_tile) tuples to amortize weight loads across pooled-spatial tiles, since weights (128*64*9 = 73K floats = 288KB) are reused N*POH*POW times.
